_comment: Acceptance-criteria manifest, mirrored out of 8090 Software Factory.
Source of truth is the factory (project b415065f-ab2f-4f53-8864-0c009fd098cb);
this file is a checked-in mirror so CI can enforce traceability without
network or MCP access. Refresh it with `make ac-sync` (agent-driven, see
FLYWHEEL.md 1g) -- never hand-edit a criterion's text to make a check pass.
Every criterion listed here must be referenced by at least one test under
tests/ (in a docstring, a marker, or the test name). scripts/check_ac_coverage.py
enforces that with a ratchet: coverage may never regress.
_scope: Only AC families this repository actually implements are gated here.
The factory also holds AC-CLOUD-*, AC-BUILD-*, AC-DEVICE-* and AC-WEB-*
criteria; those are implemented in clawmetry-cloud, the hosted builder,
clawmetry-mac/firmware and the marketing site respectively. They are listed
under external_prefixes so a stray reference to one is not mistaken for a typo.

criteria.doc: Advanced Governance
criteria.text: When an entitled extended runtime is available, the system shall observe its activity alongside the free runtimes.

criteria.doc: Advanced Governance
criteria.text: If an operator is not entitled to an extended runtime, then the system shall communicate the entitlement boundary rather than presenting the runtime as observed.

criteria.doc: Advanced Governance
criteria.text: When an extended runtime lacks a known value, the system shall preserve what it can identify without inventing the missing value.

criteria.doc: Advanced Governance
criteria.text: When the user selects a supported compliance framework, the system shall present the controls it can assess.

criteria.doc: Advanced Governance
criteria.text: When the user requests an evidence bundle, the system shall produce the evidence it holds for the selected framework.

criteria.doc: Advanced Governance
criteria.text: The system shall identify the bundle as supporting evidence rather than as a certification.

criteria.doc: Advanced Governance
criteria.text: If required evidence is unavailable, then the system shall identify the gap rather than presenting the control as satisfied.

criteria.doc: Advanced Governance
criteria.text: When an evaluation is run for eligible agent activity, the system shall record its result against the evaluated activity.

criteria.doc: Advanced Governance
criteria.text: When the system identifies an automation finding, the system shall present the finding with the evidence that produced it.

criteria.doc: Advanced Governance
criteria.text: When an action can change an agent environment, the system shall require explicit operator initiation.

criteria.doc: Advanced Evaluation and Automation
criteria.text: When an eligible assessment completes, the system shall record its result against the evaluated activity.

criteria.doc: Advanced Evaluation and Automation
criteria.text: If adequate evidence is unavailable, then the system shall report the assessment as inconclusive rather than as passed.

criteria.doc: Advanced Evaluation and Automation
criteria.text: When the system identifies a remediation finding, the system shall present the finding with its supporting evidence.

criteria.doc: Advanced Evaluation and Automation
criteria.text: When an operator requests a supported remediation action, the system shall report its accepted, rejected, or failed outcome.

criteria.doc: Advanced Evaluation and Automation
criteria.text: The system shall not apply a remediation action without explicit operator initiation.

criteria.doc: Compliance Evidence
criteria.text: When the auditor selects a supported framework, the system shall present the controls it can assess from retained evidence.

criteria.doc: Compliance Evidence
criteria.text: When a control lacks necessary evidence, the system shall identify the evidence gap.

criteria.doc: Compliance Evidence
criteria.text: The system shall not represent a control assessment as a formal certification.

criteria.doc: Compliance Evidence
criteria.text: When an auditor requests an evidence export, the system shall produce the retained records for the requested scope.

criteria.doc: Compliance Evidence
criteria.text: If a requested record is unavailable, then the system shall identify the omission in the export.

criteria.doc: Extended Runtime Support
criteria.text: When an entitled supported runtime is detected, the system shall observe and normalize its activity into the common model.

criteria.doc: Extended Runtime Support
criteria.text: If the runtime adapter cannot read a required data source, then the system shall report the unavailable source without presenting partial data as complete.

criteria.doc: Extended Runtime Support
criteria.text: When the extension is absent or not entitled, the system shall communicate the availability boundary.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: When an active require_approval policy applies to cursor or copilot, ClawMetry installs the runtime's native pre-tool hook and removes it when no policy wants it; foreign hook entries are never modified.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: Each gated runtime posts to its own pre-tool receiver URL and its approval rows carry that runtime; policies are runtime-scope filtered before matching.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: The gate is fail-open end to end: any client or server failure results in 'no opinion' and the runtime's own permission flow proceeds; a broken ClawMetry can never stall the calling agent.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: A deny decision reaches the agent with the operator's reason, in the runtime's own response contract.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: Runtime-scoped policy selection sits inside the same fail-open guard as policy loading and matching: a selection failure answers 'allow' with a stated reason.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: A runtime hosting sessions in more than one execution model is classified per session, never wholly available: it is named explicitly as split-support, so the safe default for a session that cannot be placed is refusal.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: When activity is available from a supported runtime, the system shall present the associated sessions and activity records to the operator.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: When a session contains messages, tool activity, or trace activity, the system shall present those records in the session context.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: If no supported runtime activity is available, then the system shall indicate that no activity is available and provide setup-oriented guidance.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: When new activity becomes available, the system shall make it available without requiring the operator to recreate the observed runtime.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: When the operator opens the local observability experience, the system shall present available session, usage, health, and scheduled-work status.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: When a supported runtime has active work, the system shall identify the runtime and its active session state.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: If a required local data source is unavailable, then the system shall identify the unavailable source without presenting unavailable data as current.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: When the system recognizes a supported runtime, the system shall associate its activity with that runtime.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: When runtime-specific information is unavailable, the system shall preserve the activity that it can identify without inventing missing values.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Where an extended runtime integration requires the paid extension, the system shall communicate the availability boundary before the operator relies on it.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: For every supported runtime, the system shall report a session's current phase using one shared vocabulary -- waiting on a person, working, idle, or ended -- so that sessions from different runtimes can be compared and ordered together.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Where the observed data cannot determine a session's phase, the system shall report the phase as unknown, and shall not report it as idle or as ended.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: The system shall report how long a session has been in its current phase, measured from the transition into it, and that duration shall continue to be measured from the transition after the observing service restarts.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: The system shall treat a phase as active only where it has been declared active, so that a phase value the system does not recognise is reported as not active.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Where a session has ended, the system shall report why it ended, distinguishing a session that concluded from one that went stale, one whose process is gone, and one that was archived, and shall not report an abandoned session as a concluded one.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: The system shall report the directory a session was launched in, recorded when the session is first observed and not rewritten afterwards, so that a later comparison against where the session is running is possible.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Where a session is waiting on a person, the system shall report whether that ask can be answered through ClawMetry, so that a surface never offers an action it cannot perform.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: The system shall record each received telemetry record at the time the record itself reports, and shall use the time of receipt only when the record carries no time of its own.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: The system shall retain the identity carried on a received record -- the person, their organisation, and the session -- together with any team or repository the sender declared.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Received telemetry shall be readable after a restart of the service that received it.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: The system shall report spend and token totals grouped by team, by repository, or by person, from received records alone. Every such answer shall state that the grouping is self-reported by the sender.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Re-delivery of a batch already received shall not change any reported total, in stored records or in the live view.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Where the same session is observed both from the machine and from received telemetry, the system shall report it once, and shall prefer the machine's own observation.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Tool decisions and tool results arriving as telemetry shall be usable by the trajectory detectors, so that a stuck or repeatedly failing agent is visible on a machine with nothing installed on it. A permission the user REFUSED shall not be reported as a tool the agent ran.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Where this path is described to a customer, the description shall state which runtimes it covers and that records arrive unencrypted.

criteria.doc: Project attribution and per-project budgets: burn against budget
criteria.text: The system shall attribute each session's spend to a project derived from where the session ran or from an operator assignment, and shall report for each project the source it came from and a confidence. A project or tenant name carried inside an agent's own activity shall not determine attribution.

criteria.doc: Project attribution and per-project budgets: burn against budget
criteria.text: Sessions that ran in two different repositories shall be reported as two projects even when the repositories share a directory name, and shall be combined only by an explicit operator assignment.

criteria.doc: Project attribution and per-project budgets: burn against budget
criteria.text: Spend from sessions whose working directory is unknown shall be reported in a visible unassigned group, with its amount and session count, rather than dropped or attributed to a default project.

criteria.doc: Project attribution and per-project budgets: burn against budget
criteria.text: Attribution shall be derived when read rather than stored on activity records, so an assignment applies to history already collected. Each assignment shall carry the period it is effective for, who made it, when and why, and a correction shall be recorded as a new assignment that supersedes the earlier one without erasing it.

criteria.doc: Project attribution and per-project budgets: burn against budget
criteria.text: Project figures the system publishes shall identify a project by a label and an opaque identifier, and shall not include the full local path it was derived from.

criteria.doc: Project attribution and per-project budgets: burn against budget
criteria.text: A project budget shall declare its amount, period, timezone, currency and the financial basis of the spend it is measured against. The system shall refuse a budget whose currency or timezone it cannot honour rather than silently substituting another.

criteria.doc: Project attribution and per-project budgets: burn against budget
criteria.text: Spend shall count toward the budget period in which it occurred, on the budget's own timezone, so a session running across a period boundary is split between the two periods and a record that arrives late counts in the period it occurred in.

criteria.doc: Project attribution and per-project budgets: burn against budget
criteria.text: When a project's spend in a period reaches 50%, 80% or 100% of its budget, the system shall record an alert once per threshold per period, deliver it to the operator, and state that the alert is a notification that does not stop or reverse any charge.

criteria.doc: Project attribution and per-project budgets: burn against budget
criteria.text: The budget status shall report spend for each day of the current period next to the budget, so burn can be compared against it.

criteria.doc: Project attribution and per-project budgets: burn against budget
criteria.text: The per-project export shall include assigned, unassigned and unpriced amounts and a completeness figure. Usage that carries tokens but no price shall be counted as unpriced, never as zero cost.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When cost or usage is available, the system shall present it with its associated runtime, session, or time scope.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When a cost value cannot be determined, the system shall identify it as unavailable rather than report a zero value.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When the operator changes the available time scope, the system shall update the displayed measurements to that scope.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: Where a runtime records cost for only part of its work, the system shall present the figure it has AND identify it as a floor rather than a total. Suppressing it would understate real spend; presenting it plainly would overstate what is known.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When the system identifies an efficiency signal, the system shall present the signal with its associated activity context.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: If the supporting activity is no longer available, then the system shall identify the efficiency signal as lacking current supporting context.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When prompt caching is in use, the system shall present the cache hit rate as an efficiency signal with the amount already saved and a conservative estimate of the amount left on the table, and shall label the estimate as an estimate rather than as a measured value.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When a model in observed use has a safe cheaper same-provider sibling that would fit the observed workload, the system shall present a routing recommendation with the current model, the suggested model, the observed call volume, and the estimated monthly savings, and shall reconcile the recommendation's scope with the active runtime filter.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When automatic model downgrades have already occurred, the system shall present the already-realised savings alongside the potential-savings recommendation without conflating the two.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When a finding is reported, the system shall present an estimate of the cost of the flagged period rather than the total cost of the session.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: The system shall state how each estimate was arrived at, and shall distinguish a measured figure from an approximation.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When cost cannot be determined, the system shall report it as unavailable rather than present a figure.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: The system shall order lists of findings by that estimate, and where estimates are equal shall fall back to how serious the finding is.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: An approximation shall not raise the seriousness of a finding; only a measured figure shall.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When only part of a list is shown to an operator, the system shall show the most costly entries rather than the most recent.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: The system shall record, for each session, how much work it did and where it reached, so that later sessions can be compared against it.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: Re-examining a session that is still running shall update that session's record rather than add another.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When a population has never exhibited a behaviour the system relies on observing, the system shall stop reporting the absence of that behaviour as a finding for that population.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: The system shall retain these records for a bounded period and discard older ones.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: The system shall report the cost of an agent's work alongside whether that work reached a merged change, reached a branch only, or reached neither.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: The system shall never modify a repository it reads: no checkout, no fetch, no configuration change, and no write of any kind.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: When a pull-request host is unavailable or its tooling is not installed, the system shall report what local branch and merge state supports and shall state that pull-request state is unavailable, rather than failing or omitting the surface.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: Every reported figure shall carry the basis it was derived from, and a figure resting on an uncertain correlation shall be reported as uncertain rather than presented next to certain ones.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: Spend on abandoned work shall be counted only for sessions whose runtime reported that they ended. An inactive session shall not be treated as an abandoned one.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: Sessions whose working directory is unknown shall be reported as not attributable, with a count, rather than silently dropped from the totals.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: Outcomes shall be attributed to a runtime, a model or a repository, and shall not be attributed to a named person.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: A named window of time on this surface shall mean the same span as the same-named window on every other cost surface.

criteria.doc: Cost and Efficiency Analytics
criteria.text: Reading a repository shall be bounded in how much history it examines and in how long it may take, and shall be capable of being switched off entirely on a node.

criteria.doc: Cost Optimizer: honest, fast and provider-aware
criteria.text: When the operator opens the Cost Optimizer, the system shall show a loading state, and if no answer arrives within a bounded time the system shall replace it with a plain-language sentence and a way to retry, never a raw error code and never an unending spinner.

criteria.doc: Cost Optimizer: honest, fast and provider-aware
criteria.text: When the operator is not entitled to the Cost Optimizer, the system shall show an upgrade prompt rather than presenting the refusal as missing data.

criteria.doc: Cost Optimizer: honest, fast and provider-aware
criteria.text: Every cost figure the optimizer shows shall carry its basis (measured, derived, estimated, or unavailable), and a figure the system could not determine shall be shown as unavailable rather than as zero.

criteria.doc: Cost Optimizer: honest, fast and provider-aware
criteria.text: The optimizer shall not present a savings amount or percentage that was not computed from this operator's observed usage, and shall present each recommendation as an experiment to try, citing the observed usage it is based on.

criteria.doc: Cost Optimizer: honest, fast and provider-aware
criteria.text: When observed traffic runs through a managed or hosted model provider and none runs through a local model, the system shall not recommend running models locally, and shall say why that advice is hidden.

criteria.doc: Cost Optimizer: honest, fast and provider-aware
criteria.text: The optimizer shall be reachable from the Usage tab without scrolling at a typical laptop viewport.

criteria.doc: Cost Optimizer: honest, fast and provider-aware
criteria.text: When the operator views a past moment in time-travel mode, the system shall state that the optimizer analyses current spend and where historical spend can be reviewed, rather than showing a placeholder.

criteria.doc: Cost Optimizer: honest, fast and provider-aware
criteria.text: When the token count behind a cost row was not recorded, the system shall say the token count was not recorded rather than label the row "unknown tokens".

criteria.doc: Cost Optimizer: honest, fast and provider-aware
criteria.text: When the operator opens the Cost Optimizer on the hosted dashboard, the system shall show the same experiments, local-model advice and basis-labelled figures that the local dashboard derives for that computer from its recorded usage, computed on that computer and readable only in the operator's browser; and when the connected computer does not yet send them, the system shall say so rather than show recommendations that cite no observed usage or figures without a basis.

criteria.doc: Cost Optimizer: honest, fast and provider-aware
criteria.text: When the operator has scoped the dashboard to one runtime, the Cost Optimizer shall show only that runtime's recorded spend, expensive calls and experiments and shall name the runtime its figures cover; and when that runtime has no recorded spend, or the connected computer does not yet send figures per runtime, the system shall show the figures as unavailable rather than another runtime's or the whole computer's.

criteria.doc: Cost basis labels: usage value at published rates, contract spend and actual spend are never confused
criteria.text: Each cost figure on the Overview spend tile; on the Usage tab's period cost cards, Cost Breakdown table, subscription coverage banner, both Top Sessions by Cost tables and the session cost chart; on the Flow brain panel's cost card and per-call cost list; and in the hosted snapshot's cost slice shall carry a financial basis of exactly one of: usage value at published rates, expected contract spend, allocated actual spend, or unavailable, shown as visible text beside the figure or on the heading or caption of the column, list or chart that holds it.

criteria.doc: Cost basis labels: usage value at published rates, contract spend and actual spend are never confused
criteria.text: The system shall not label a figure expected contract spend unless it records the contract rate version it was priced from, and shall not label a figure allocated actual spend unless it records the invoice or billing-ledger reference it was drawn from; a request for either label without that evidence shall produce an unavailable basis with the reason, never a silently upgraded label.

criteria.doc: Cost basis labels: usage value at published rates, contract spend and actual spend are never confused
criteria.text: A cost the runtime reported itself shall be identified as the runtime's own figure (its source), and shall still be labelled usage value at published rates rather than actual spend.

criteria.doc: Cost basis labels: usage value at published rates, contract spend and actual spend are never confused
criteria.text: Where a subscription is detected, the Usage tab shall show the API-equivalent value of subscription-covered usage separately from usage on metered routes, and shall never present the subscription-covered value as an additional bill nor state that the covered usage cost the operator nothing.

criteria.doc: Cost basis labels: usage value at published rates, contract spend and actual spend are never confused
criteria.text: Where the billing route of part of the usage was not detected, the system shall label that part's route as not detected rather than as metered or as covered.

criteria.doc: Cost basis labels: usage value at published rates, contract spend and actual spend are never confused
criteria.text: Where the provider does not expose the plan fee, included allowance or overage to ClawMetry, the system shall say that those are not included rather than show them as zero.

criteria.doc: Cost basis labels: usage value at published rates, contract spend and actual spend are never confused
criteria.text: Hovering or keyboard-focusing a basis label shall show how the figure was computed: the formula, the source of the rate, the window, and the billing route where one applies.

criteria.doc: Cost basis labels: usage value at published rates, contract spend and actual spend are never confused
criteria.text: Each cost figure on the Overview hero chip; on the Usage tab's Where the money goes chart, Cost Forecast, Cache Re-read Tax, cache hit rate and cache performance cards, savings ideas and routing advisor cards, compression potential card, Cost By Plugin / Skill, Cost Comparison, Spend Optimization, Skill Cost Leaderboard and Cost by Team cards; and on the per-turn and per-tool cost chips of a Sessions tab transcript shall carry a financial basis of exactly one of the four in AC-OBS-CEA-025.1, shown as visible text beside the figure or on the heading or caption of the card, chart, list or transcript that holds it. The payloads that serve these figures, including the hosted snapshot slices the hosted dashboard reads them from (efficiency, spend flow, forecast, cost comparison, cache trends, spend optimization and transcripts), shall carry the same basis.

criteria.doc: Cost basis labels: usage value at published rates, contract spend and actual spend are never confused
criteria.text: A counterfactual cost figure (a projected saving, a month-end forecast, or what the same usage would cost on another model) shall be labelled an estimate of usage value at published rates, and no card shall describe usage value at published rates as actual spend.

criteria.doc: Cost basis labels: usage value at published rates, contract spend and actual spend are never confused
criteria.text: The count of dollar figures rendered without a basis on the Overview, Usage and Sessions tabs shall not increase; the check shall find those renders from the tabs' own templates rather than from a hand-kept list.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: When an operator creates or changes a valid policy, the system shall retain the policy for its authorized scope.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: When an operator evaluates a policy against historical activity, the system shall show the resulting candidate matches without changing historical activity.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: If a policy is invalid, then the system shall identify the invalid policy without enabling it.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: When an approval request is pending, the system shall present its available action context and decision options to an authorized approver.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: When an approver decides a pending request, the system shall record the decision outcome and make it visible to the relevant workflow.

criteria.doc: Governance and Human Approval
criteria.text: If a request is expired, already decided, or unavailable, then the system shall not accept a new decision.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: When the operator requests integrity verification, the system shall report whether the retained records pass or fail the available integrity check.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: If integrity verification finds an unexpected record change, then the system shall identify that the verification failed.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: When every retained record still matches its own recorded fingerprint but the records cannot be arranged into a single ordered chain, the system shall report a third outcome, distinct from both pass and fail, and shall state that no record was altered or removed.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: The system shall report verification failure only when a record's stored content no longer matches its recorded fingerprint, or when a record names a predecessor that is absent from the log. Incomplete ordering alone shall not be reported as failure.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: When cloud synchronization is not configured, the system shall continue to provide local observability without requiring cloud access.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: When the operator enables cloud synchronization, the system shall communicate the information category and protection boundary associated with the synchronization.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: When the operator disables cloud synchronization, the system shall stop new optional synchronization activity.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: The system shall not send a transcript excerpt to a third-party model for quality scoring unless the operator has turned scoring on for the node. The presence of a model provider credential in the environment shall not count as consent.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: The system shall record every cloud-relayed action in the node's local audit log when it arrives, whether it is then carried out or refused, so the operator holds their own record of what the service asked of the machine. The record shall name the action and its identifiers and shall not store the action body.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: A request the node makes to the cloud service shall carry the account credential in a request header, never in the request URL.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: The system shall not include a runtime's configuration files, meaning hook settings, MCP server manifests and gateway configuration, in any upload to the cloud service, encrypted or not. Such files may remain in the local catalog.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: The system shall present the retention period currently in force for local activity history, and shall state which setting is producing it.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: The operator shall be able to shorten the retention period, and the choice shall persist on the node across restarts.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: The system shall never lengthen retention beyond the entitlement's ceiling. A request for a longer period shall be recorded as requested but shall not extend what is kept, and the system shall report both the requested and the enforced period.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: The system shall reject a retention value that is not a whole number of days of at least one, rather than substituting a default.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: The component that deletes aged history shall use the same resolved period the system reports to the operator.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: The operator shall be able to clear their choice and return to the entitlement's period.

criteria.doc: Local Audit and Data Control
criteria.text: Before shortening the retention period, the system shall state what will be deleted and that the deletion is permanent, and shall require confirmation. Raising the period, or returning to the plan's period, destroys nothing and shall not require confirmation.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When the operator selects an available session, the system shall present its ordered activity records.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When an activity record has associated tool input, result, or error information, the system shall present the available associated information in that session context.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: If the selected session has no recorded activity, then the system shall indicate that the session is empty.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When trace information is available for an operation, the system shall present its related activity records in their available relationship.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: If trace information is incomplete, then the system shall identify the available records without implying complete coverage.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: Family adapters emit each spawned child as a session with a parent link and a kind of sub-agent, workflow run, or workflow agent; the sync daemon records these on the subagents table via an explicit whitelist into the row's data blob.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: Still-running children are re-read on every sync pass so their live status never goes stale; child transcript events are ingested under the child's own namespaced session id.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: GET /api/session-orchestration/<session_id> returns the full orchestration tree for one session, accepting bare or runtime-prefixed ids, from the local store only, with an honest empty tree otherwise.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: GET /api/orchestration-summary?session_ids=... returns bulk per-session counts without prompt or reply text, backed by query_subagents_lite and exposed through the daemon query proxy allowlist.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: The Activity feed offers per-session filter chips that work on the local-store fast path, labels child runs as sub-agent or workflow-agent blocks, and shows an orchestration badge per session block.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: The Sessions tab transcript viewer includes an Orchestration panel with expandable per-agent 'Context given' and 'Replied' blocks; it auto-expands while anything is still running.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: A workflow-run row carries no tokens or cost of its own; its agents own their usage, so orchestration rollups never double-count.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: OpenClaw sub-agent and flow registries in state/openclaw.sqlite are mirrored into the subagents table; the subagents data blob merges across writers so no pass erases another's fields.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: Only genuine delegations carry a parent link. Forks, compression continuations and resume seeds keep their lineage in the session's extra data with no parent id.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When an agent mutates an unusual number of files for its history, or runs a destructive command such as a recursive delete at a home or system root, the system shall report it while the session is still running.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When an agent opens a credential bearing artefact, the system shall report the CATEGORY of what was opened and shall not record its path.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When an agent contacts an external destination it has no history of contacting, the system shall report it, and shall stay silent on that ground until it has enough history to make the claim.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When an agent escalates privilege or weakens a system protection, the system shall report it, and shall distinguish actions that outlive the session from ordinary elevation.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: Every report derived from tool arguments shall state that origin, so that no reader mistakes it for kernel level observation.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When a pattern appears inside a document the agent wrote, or inside a command that only inspects text, the system shall not report it as an action.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: No report shall contain a full command line or a full filesystem path.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When a runtime records file changes in a form the system can observe, the system shall treat those changes as progress for that runtime, including where the change is made through a shell command.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When a population of comparable sessions is too small to characterise, the system shall apply its shipped defaults rather than a measurement.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When a measurement is used, the system shall bound it so that neither an unusually busy population nor an unusually quiet one can disable or saturate reporting.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: The system shall state, for each reported finding, whether the threshold it crossed was measured or shipped.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: When an operator sets a threshold for a specific runtime, the system shall prefer that value over both the shipped default and any measurement.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: The system shall attribute a session to the runtime that produced it, and shall not rely on a stored value that can disagree with the session's own identity.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: The system shall not transmit a session title to the hosted service in a form that service can read.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: The system shall carry session titles to the hosted dashboard by the same encrypted path as other session content, keyed so that a title can be matched to the session it belongs to.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: Where a session has no title of its own, the system shall carry nothing rather than an identifier presented as a title.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: A failure to produce titles shall degrade to no titles, and shall never prevent the rest of the snapshot from being produced.

criteria.doc: Coordinated action: unrelated sessions acting in step
criteria.text: The system shall describe each observed write as an action made of its method or transfer type, its destination, and the first two segments of its path, with any path segment containing a digit masked, so that per-agent directory names collapse into the shared location they sit under.

criteria.doc: Coordinated action: unrelated sessions acting in step
criteria.text: When sessions from at least a configured number of unrelated families (default five) perform the same action that the node has no settled history of, the system shall raise one finding for that action, naming the action and how many families took it.

criteria.doc: Coordinated action: unrelated sessions acting in step
criteria.text: Sessions linked by a parent/child (orchestrator/subagent) relationship, including through several levels or a cycle, shall count as one family.

criteria.doc: Coordinated action: unrelated sessions acting in step
criteria.text: An action counts as normal only after it has been in the node's memory for the settle window; an action first seen inside the window stays unusual, so the first member of a swarm cannot vouch for the rest.

criteria.doc: Coordinated action: unrelated sessions acting in step
criteria.text: A node that has not been recording actions for a full settle window shall raise no such finding.

criteria.doc: Coordinated action: unrelated sessions acting in step
criteria.text: Each finding shall reach a person as one message, however many sessions share it, and shall appear on each participating session in the Guard tab without being re-recorded on every tick.

criteria.doc: Coordinated action: unrelated sessions acting in step
criteria.text: A policy that does not name this kind shall not act on it, so a catch-all rule written about single agents cannot pause every participant at once.

criteria.doc: Coordinated action: unrelated sessions acting in step
criteria.text: The finding shall state that it is derived from tool arguments.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: Session records persist the working directory and git branch when the runtime records them (first-class fields on the session row); an unavailable directory stays empty, never fabricated.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: The first-class cwd field is the contract consumers act on; an adapter's mirror of the same value in extra metadata is compatibility-and-diagnostic only for older wheels.

criteria.doc: Runtime and Session Observability
criteria.text: Family-runtime event rows carry the session's working directory as their workspace attribution so approval deny-kills can resolve cwd-based runtimes.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Report, for a repository named by the operator or discovered from session history, a grade for how legible that repository is to an agent, covering instruction file, test command, build command, lint or format gate, CI configuration and repository-scoped agent skills.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Report, beside that grade and for the same repository, how many sessions ran there in a stated window and how many of them the detectors recorded as stuck.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Report every passing check with the specific path that was read to reach that verdict, and every failing check with the paths that were looked for plus a remediation the operator can act on.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Report a check whose input could not be read as an explicit unknown that does not affect the grade in either direction, rather than as a failure or a pass.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Report a repository with no recorded session history as having no history, distinctly from a repository where sessions ran and none got stuck.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Report, per runtime, which runtimes would find their instructions in the repository, and scope the graded result to the runtime the operator has selected.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Complete without making any network request and without executing any command from the repository under examination.

criteria.doc: Local Agent Observability
criteria.text: Remain available on every plan, including free, with no entitlement gate.

criteria.doc: Onboarding Gate Funnel Visibility
criteria.text: When the dashboard resolves that an onboarding choice is required and serves that state to a browser, the system shall send one install lifecycle ping with event gate_shown carrying the same anonymous fields as the install ping.

criteria.doc: Onboarding Gate Funnel Visibility
criteria.text: When the gate state is served again for the same install, the system shall not send a second gate_shown ping, regardless of how many browser sessions or page reloads occur.

criteria.doc: Onboarding Gate Funnel Visibility
criteria.text: When telemetry is opted out by any existing mechanism (environment variable, do-not-track, marker file), the system shall not send the gate_shown ping.

criteria.doc: Onboarding Gate Funnel Visibility
criteria.text: When the ping fails for any reason, the system shall serve the gate state unchanged and shall not surface an error to the user.

criteria.doc: Onboarding Gate Funnel Visibility
criteria.text: When the hosted cloud dashboard serves onboarding state, the system shall not send a gate_shown ping, because hosted accounts never see the gate.

criteria.doc: Every Account Knows Whether It Is Cloud or Self-Hosted
criteria.text: When a person signs in from the terminal and chooses to sync data to ClawMetry Cloud, the install shall report deployment `managed` on the trial sign-in call.

criteria.doc: Every Account Knows Whether It Is Cloud or Self-Hosted
criteria.text: When a person signs in from the terminal and chooses to keep data on the machine, the install shall report deployment `selfhost` on the trial sign-in call.

criteria.doc: Every Account Knows Whether It Is Cloud or Self-Hosted
criteria.text: When a person signs in through the local dashboard's cloud sign-in, the install shall report `managed`; through its keep-local sign-in, `selfhost`.

criteria.doc: Every Account Knows Whether It Is Cloud or Self-Hosted
criteria.text: When the report cannot be delivered or the cloud rejects it, sign-in and trial activation shall complete exactly as they would without it.

criteria.doc: Claude Code Native Telemetry: One-Command OTel Wiring + Full Signal Mapping
criteria.text: `clawmetry instrument claude` writes the Claude Code telemetry block into the env object of the settings file (user or --project), merging without clobbering keys it did not write, idempotently, with protocol http/json and the endpoint of whichever local receiver is listening; --uninstall removes only keys it wrote; it states that running sessions keep their old configuration until restarted.

criteria.doc: Claude Code Native Telemetry: One-Command OTel Wiring + Full Signal Mapping
criteria.text: Content flags (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT) are off unless --content is passed; OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES is never written.

criteria.doc: Claude Code Native Telemetry: One-Command OTel Wiring + Full Signal Mapping
criteria.text: On a machine where Claude Code managed settings lock the OTLP destination, the command refuses and says so; it never leaves a half-written block.

criteria.doc: Claude Code Native Telemetry: One-Command OTel Wiring + Full Signal Mapping
criteria.text: Every claude_code.* metric is mapped: token usage by type (input, output, cacheRead, cacheCreation) with model, cost, session count, lines of code, commits, pull requests, active time and edit-tool decisions; cache tokens land in the same cache fields the JSONL path fills.

criteria.doc: Claude Code Native Telemetry: One-Command OTel Wiring + Full Signal Mapping
criteria.text: Every Claude Code event is retained with its typed fields and surfaced: permission decisions with source, permission-mode changes, API refusals, API errors, MCP server connection status, auth events, user-prompt and assistant-response lengths; a rejected tool decision is never recorded as a tool call.

criteria.doc: Claude Code Native Telemetry: One-Command OTel Wiring + Full Signal Mapping
criteria.text: Tracing-beta spans render with real durations: LLM request spans carry input/output/cache tokens under Claude Code's attribute names, tool spans carry the tool name, and tool.blocked_on_user is surfaced as time waiting on you per session and per turn.

criteria.doc: Claude Code Native Telemetry: One-Command OTel Wiring + Full Signal Mapping
criteria.text: A session observed by both the daemon and the exporter is one session: transcript cost and tokens remain authoritative and are never added twice; OTel-only fields attach to that session with a provenance marker.

criteria.doc: Claude Code Native Telemetry: One-Command OTel Wiring + Full Signal Mapping
criteria.text: `clawmetry status` and /api/otel-status report whether the Claude Code exporter is configured, at which path and endpoint, and when the last Claude Code batch arrived, so a silently dropped batch is visible.

criteria.doc: Claude Code Native Telemetry: One-Command OTel Wiring + Full Signal Mapping
criteria.text: docs/enterprise.md and docs/OPENTELEMETRY.md name CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY, state that Claude Code has no default protocol, and show the block the command writes.

criteria.doc: Claude Code Native Telemetry: One-Command OTel Wiring + Full Signal Mapping
criteria.text: Claude Code is a paid runtime: the instrument command and every Claude Code specific mapping (session join, typed events, cache token tiles, waiting-on-you, span materialization) follow the claude_code runtime entitlement; without it the receiver still accepts batches and keeps only the generic ledger and span rows, and the command reports the plan requirement instead of writing.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: The system shall accept a local price book whose entries identify a model exactly, by prefix, or by a validated pattern, carry an effective start date, and state either explicit per-token rates or a percentage discount off the published rate.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: The system shall reject each malformed entry, and each pair of entries that would claim the same usage over overlapping dates, with a stated reason per entry, and shall continue to accept the valid remainder of the book rather than failing it whole.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: When more than one valid entry could apply to a usage record and the documented precedence does not separate them, the system shall report the record as ambiguous and shall not choose a rate.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: An entry shall apply to usage observed at or after its effective start and strictly before its effective end; usage with no observed time shall not be matched to a dated rate.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: The system shall resolve an Azure OpenAI deployment name to a model through an explicit alias, scoped to its resource where the alias names one, and shall prefer that alias over a model name reported by the response.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: The system shall resolve AWS Bedrock model identifiers, including region prefixes, vendor prefixes and version suffixes, to the same model a price book entry names.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: Every edit to the price book shall produce a new version identifier; a version once recorded shall never be altered; and resolving usage against an earlier version shall return the rate that version held.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: When no published rate exists for a model and no price book entry applies, the system shall report the price as unknown rather than substitute a generic default rate.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: Every valuation the system returns shall state its basis (vendor reported, contract, list, default or unknown), the rate version and effective interval it used, and whether it restates an earlier valuation; a valuation lacking these shall not be returned.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: For each usage record, the system shall state whether that source counts cached input tokens inside its input token total, so that a valuation neither adds nor subtracts them twice.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: The price book, its rates and its recorded versions shall remain on the machine where they were written, and no path that sends data off the machine shall read them.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: When the price book version in effect at the time usage was observed selects exactly one entry for that usage and a valuation engine is present, the local Usage view shall show that usage valued at the contract rate, labelled as contract rate and naming the recorded book version; a figure whose book version is not recorded shall not be labelled contract, and the published-rate figures shall stay shown beside it.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: Each usage record shall be valued against the book version that was in effect when it was observed. A later edit to the book shall not change the figure shown for usage observed before the edit, unless the user explicitly asks for a restatement; a restated figure shall be labelled as a restatement and shown beside the original amount.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: Usage for which the applicable entries are ambiguous, or which no rate can price, shall be counted and shown as unknown with its reason, and shall add no amount to a contract figure.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: The local dashboard shall provide a price book screen showing the validated entries, the aliases, each rejected entry with its reasons, and the recorded versions with the time each came into effect, and shall let the user add an entry or edit an existing one.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: An entry edit shall be validated before it is saved; each problem shall be shown as a readable sentence beside the field it concerns; nothing shall be written without an explicit save; a save shall be refused when the book changed after it was loaded; and a successful save shall report the new version and the time from which it applies.

criteria.doc: Price Book: negotiated rates, deployment aliases and effective dates
criteria.text: Usage facts shall be stored once, as the recorded usage events, and contract valuations shall be derived when read; no valuation shall be written back into stored usage, and no process that sends data off the machine shall compute or carry one.

criteria.doc: Exported traces reach Guard, and are scrubbed before they are stored
criteria.text: When a received trace contains a span describing a tool call in a known session, the system shall record it as a tool call, and a tool result, that the detectors evaluate exactly as they evaluate a machine-observed tool call, and each recorded event shall retain the trace, span and session it came from.

criteria.doc: Exported traces reach Guard, and are scrubbed before they are stored
criteria.text: The system shall not record a tool call for a span that does not identify itself as a tool execution or that belongs to no session, and where a tool span does not carry its arguments, the system shall not treat that call as identical to any other call.

criteria.doc: Exported traces reach Guard, and are scrubbed before they are stored
criteria.text: Where the tool calls of one session arrive both as log records and as trace spans, or are also observed on the machine, the system shall record them from one source only, so that no tool call is counted twice.

criteria.doc: Exported traces reach Guard, and are scrubbed before they are stored
criteria.text: Before a received span is stored, the system shall apply the secret and personal-data redaction it applies to observed events to the span's prompts, responses, tool arguments, attributes (including URLs and paths), span events (including exception events), links, name and status message, and the same redaction shall apply to the attributes kept in the received log-record ledger.

criteria.doc: Exported traces reach Guard, and are scrubbed before they are stored
criteria.text: Where a span value cannot be scanned, because it is too large or the scanner fails, the system shall withhold that value and mark the span as withheld rather than store it unscanned. Where the operator has turned redaction off, spans shall be stored as received, as events are.

criteria.doc: Exported traces reach Guard, and are scrubbed before they are stored
criteria.text: An incident raised only from received telemetry shall state that the action was observed after it ran and shall not state or imply that the action was prevented.

criteria.doc: Exported traces reach Guard, and are scrubbed before they are stored
criteria.text: When an incident is raised on a node from received telemetry and the node is connected to the hosted dashboard, the hosted Guard tab shall list that session with the incident, under the runtime its telemetry names (so a runtime filter finds it), with the observed-after-the-fact label, and shall show the session as not controllable from any machine with a sentence saying why, rather than offering Pause, Stop or Kill.

criteria.doc: Exported traces reach Guard, and are scrubbed before they are stored
criteria.text: Where the same tool call, identified by the same call id, arrives both as a log record and as a trace span, the system shall record exactly one tool call and one tool result for it, taken from the trace span, whichever signal arrives first. A tool call that only one signal reports shall still be recorded. Where a call carries no call id, the system shall keep the first signal to report that session's tool calls and count the other signal's copies as skipped.

criteria.doc: Exported traces reach Guard, and are scrubbed before they are stored
criteria.text: The operator shall be able to choose how much content received telemetry keeps: `full` (content kept, secrets still masked, personal data not filtered), `redacted` (the default: content kept, secrets masked, personal data filtered per its own switches) or `metadata` (no prompt, response, argument, result or free-text attribute stored; each withheld field is labelled on the stored row). Secret masking shall follow only its own switch under every profile, personal-data filtering shall remain separately switchable, and the security posture shall state the active profile, what it keeps, and which personal data is not detected.

criteria.doc: Exported traces reach Guard, and are scrubbed before they are stored
criteria.text: Spans stored before scrubbing existed shall not be rewritten unless the operator runs an explicit rescrub. The rescrub shall report how many stored spans would change without changing anything unless the operator confirms, shall rewrite only content fields, and shall report how many it rewrote and that copies already sent off the machine are unaffected.

criteria.doc: Fleet Install on Shared and Virtual Desktops
criteria.text: When a Linux user registers the collector for fleet use, the system shall request that the user's services persist after logout and report whether persistence is enabled, and if it could not be enabled, the exact administrator command that enables it.

criteria.doc: Fleet Install on Shared and Virtual Desktops
criteria.text: When an administrator registers the collector for all users on Windows, the system shall register a single logon registration that starts a separate collector as each signed-in user, and shall not run the collector under a privileged account.

criteria.doc: Fleet Install on Shared and Virtual Desktops
criteria.text: When fleet registration is removed, the system shall remove every registration it created and report what was removed.

criteria.doc: Fleet Install on Shared and Virtual Desktops
criteria.text: When the collector runs from an isolated environment that the running user cannot write (an administrator-owned fleet install), the system shall not attempt an unattended self-update or restart for one, and fleet status shall report automatic updates as off with that reason and how the install is updated instead.

criteria.doc: Fleet Install on Shared and Virtual Desktops
criteria.text: When an operator requests fleet status, the system shall report, per operating system, whether collection continues after the user logs off, and when it does not, the reason.

criteria.doc: Fleet Install on Shared and Virtual Desktops
criteria.text: When the local data directory is readable by other local users, the system shall report it as not private, and fleet registration shall restrict it to the owning user.

criteria.doc: Fleet Install on Shared and Virtual Desktops
criteria.text: The system shall provide a silent install example for Windows management tooling and one for Linux configuration management, each exercised in automated verification on that operating system.

criteria.doc: Fleet Install on Shared and Virtual Desktops
criteria.text: The install examples shall not embed an enrollment credential and shall not print one to their output.

criteria.doc: Guard ATLAS OpenClaw replay: case studies AML.CS0048 to AML.CS0051 scored against Guard
criteria.text: The system shall pin, for every replayed case study, the ATLAS edition and source revision, the case identifier and name, each procedure step with the technique identifier published for it in that edition, and the ATLAS mitigations published against those techniques (ATLAS links mitigations to techniques, not to case studies, so the case to mitigation mapping is derived and labelled as such). A source report whose revision cannot be retrieved shall be named in the scorecard as not pinned.

criteria.doc: Guard ATLAS OpenClaw replay: case studies AML.CS0048 to AML.CS0051 scored against Guard
criteria.text: For each scenario the system shall record the runtime, the evaluation tier, the policy set in force and the expected outcome of every stage.

criteria.doc: Guard ATLAS OpenClaw replay: case studies AML.CS0048 to AML.CS0051 scored against Guard
criteria.text: The system shall score every stage of every scenario as unobservable, observed, partial, detected or held before action, naming the finding kinds that fired and the timestamp of the first flagged event, and shall roll each case up to caught, partial or missed.

criteria.doc: Guard ATLAS OpenClaw replay: case studies AML.CS0048 to AML.CS0051 scored against Guard
criteria.text: A fixture replay shall never score a stage as held before action, and its results shall be labelled fixture replay, distinct from isolated execution evidence.

criteria.doc: Guard ATLAS OpenClaw replay: case studies AML.CS0048 to AML.CS0051 scored against Guard
criteria.text: The suite shall include benign controls, an intentional allow and at least one failure mode of a pre-action control, and shall report any finding on a benign control as a false positive.

criteria.doc: Guard ATLAS OpenClaw replay: case studies AML.CS0048 to AML.CS0051 scored against Guard
criteria.text: The system shall generate the scorecard from the replay, and continuous integration shall fail when the committed scorecard and the replay disagree, or when a stage outcome changes without its pinned expectation changing.

criteria.doc: Guard ATLAS OpenClaw replay: case studies AML.CS0048 to AML.CS0051 scored against Guard
criteria.text: The scorecard shall state that fixture replay does not establish protection against CVE-2026-25253 or against prompt injection in general, and shall list the residual gaps.

criteria.doc: Guard ATLAS OpenClaw replay: case studies AML.CS0048 to AML.CS0051 scored against Guard
criteria.text: The system shall produce a redacted evidence bundle that contains pins and sha256 of every fixture and stage outcomes, but no raw commands or file paths, and the bundle shall be deterministic given the same generated_at timestamp.

criteria.doc: Guard Framework References: OWASP LLM 2026, OWASP Agentic 2026 and MITRE ATLAS IDs on findings
criteria.text: When a detector, workspace or fleet finding kind exists in the product, the system shall declare for it either at least one framework reference or an explicit "none" with the reason no identifier applies.

criteria.doc: Guard Framework References: OWASP LLM 2026, OWASP Agentic 2026 and MITRE ATLAS IDs on findings
criteria.text: The system shall state one mapping version for the whole contract and, for each framework, the edition and source revision its identifiers were verified against.

criteria.doc: Guard Framework References: OWASP LLM 2026, OWASP Agentic 2026 and MITRE ATLAS IDs on findings
criteria.text: When a kind is mapped, the system shall carry a rationale, a stated limit of what the finding can and cannot establish, and references to a test that fires on the behaviour and a test that stays quiet on benign work.

criteria.doc: Guard Framework References: OWASP LLM 2026, OWASP Agentic 2026 and MITRE ATLAS IDs on findings
criteria.text: The system shall reference only identifiers present in the pinned edition of their framework, and shall keep MITRE ATLAS techniques, mitigations and case studies distinguishable.

criteria.doc: Guard Framework References: OWASP LLM 2026, OWASP Agentic 2026 and MITRE ATLAS IDs on findings
criteria.text: When the system reports a Guard finding, the finding shall carry the framework references for its kind, the mapping version and its capability mode.

criteria.doc: Guard Framework References: OWASP LLM 2026, OWASP Agentic 2026 and MITRE ATLAS IDs on findings
criteria.text: When the system lists a Guard policy decision, the decision shall carry the framework references of the finding kind it acted on and an evidence level of configured, exercised or failed; the system shall not report a decision as effective unless an independent outcome check exists.

criteria.doc: Guard Framework References: OWASP LLM 2026, OWASP Agentic 2026 and MITRE ATLAS IDs on findings
criteria.text: The system shall generate the public framework coverage document from the mapping contract, and continuous integration shall fail when the document and the contract disagree.

criteria.doc: Guard Framework References: OWASP LLM 2026, OWASP Agentic 2026 and MITRE ATLAS IDs on findings
criteria.text: The coverage document shall describe coverage and not compliance, and shall list the framework items Guard does not cover as gaps.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: When a report is requested for a commit range, the system shall link each changed file to the sessions that wrote it, recording for each link its basis (a commit trailer naming the session, or a write tool call on that path recorded by the session), and shall list changed files with no link as unattributed rather than omitting them.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: The system shall present a file-to-session link as association and not as proof that the session caused a finding on that file; every link and every annotated finding shall carry its basis.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: The system shall emit the report as SARIF 2.1.0 in which each Guard finding raised by a linked session is a result on each file that session is linked to, with its level mapped from the finding's severity (critical to error, warning to warning, anything else to note).

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: When scanner SARIF is supplied, the system shall reproduce its findings and annotate each finding located on a linked file with the session identifier, runtime, model and link basis, and shall leave findings on unlinked files unannotated. The system shall produce no finding of its own about code content.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: The SARIF, the markdown summary and the console output shall contain no prompt text, no tool output and no credential-shaped value; text copied from supplied scanner findings shall pass through secret redaction.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: The system shall produce the report from an exported provenance bundle with no local store and no network access, as well as from the local store.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: An exported bundle shall record the commits it covers and a content digest. When the digest does not match the content, or the bundle covers no commit in the evaluated range, the system shall treat the bundle as invalid evidence; when commits in the range are not covered, the system shall report them as missing evidence. The system shall state that the digest is an integrity check and not proof of authenticity.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: The gate shall be off unless explicitly enabled, and while off the report shall exit successfully whatever it finds. Enabling the gate shall require a threshold and an explicit choice of behaviour for missing, stale or invalid evidence; the system shall refuse to evaluate a gate enabled without that choice.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: When the gate is enabled, a finding at or above the threshold on a linked file shall fail the run unless an unexpired exception names it; an expired exception shall not apply and shall be reported as expired.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: Every gate evaluation shall record its outcome, rule version, threshold, evidence behaviour, actor, time, evaluated head commit and the exceptions it applied.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: When the report is posted to a pull request, the system shall maintain a single comment identified by a marker, updating it on later runs rather than adding another.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: When reading the local store, the system shall resolve a session's relative write paths only against that session's recorded working directory, and shall not link a session working in another directory or repository to the change through a relative path; a session with no recorded working directory shall be linked through a relative path only when a commit trailer in the change names it, and relative writes it cannot place that match a changed file shall be reported as missing evidence without naming the session.

criteria.doc: PR provenance report: agent sessions on changed files, as SARIF and an opt-in CI gate
criteria.text: When any read limit truncates the evidence (sessions listed, sessions read, events or Guard findings per session, or commits in the range), the system shall report the evidence as partial with the reason, both in the report and in an exported bundle, so that an enabled gate applies the operator's missing-evidence behaviour rather than passing silently.

criteria.doc: Framework recipe: a LangGraph agent instrumented with OpenLLMetry, verified end to end
criteria.text: The project shall ship a runnable minimal LangGraph agent with exactly one tool that exports OpenTelemetry through OpenLLMetry to the ClawMetry receiver and runs with no model provider key.

criteria.doc: Framework recipe: a LangGraph agent instrumented with OpenLLMetry, verified end to end
criteria.text: On every change, an automated check shall run that recipe, with its framework, instrumentation and exporter versions pinned, against a live ClawMetry instance, and shall fail unless the run is readable back through the local query API as a session under the application's identity, carrying the token totals the model reported and the tool call by name.

criteria.doc: Framework recipe: a LangGraph agent instrumented with OpenLLMetry, verified end to end
criteria.text: When a LangGraph run carries a thread identifier, the system shall record every span of that run, including the model calls and tool calls beneath the run's top span, under one session identified by that thread, and every later run on the same thread under the same session. The instrumentation reports the thread as the conversation identifier on the run's top span only, and as a thread association on every span beneath it; both shall resolve to the same session, recorded exactly as sent, so a run is never split between a session for its top span and a separate per-trace session holding its tokens and tool calls.

criteria.doc: Framework recipe: a LangGraph agent instrumented with OpenLLMetry, verified end to end
criteria.text: An explicitly sent conversation identifier shall take precedence over a thread identifier, and a thread identifier shall take precedence over a session identifier sent on the span or on the resource, so that a session identifier stamped on the spans beneath a run's top span can never split that run away from the conversation identifier its top span sends; whichever identifier wins shall be recorded exactly as sent.

criteria.doc: Framework recipe: a LangGraph agent instrumented with OpenLLMetry, verified end to end
criteria.text: When a run carries neither a conversation identifier nor a thread identifier, the system shall record one session per trace, as REQ-OBS-RSO-033 defines, and the recipe page shall name that fallback and its cardinality.

criteria.doc: Framework recipe: a LangGraph agent instrumented with OpenLLMetry, verified end to end
criteria.text: When the agent runs in streaming mode, the check shall find the same session, token totals and tool call as for a non-streaming run.

criteria.doc: Framework recipe: a LangGraph agent instrumented with OpenLLMetry, verified end to end
criteria.text: When the recipe exports to a ClawMetry on another machine, the automated check shall prove that an export without the Bearer token is refused and an export carrying it is accepted, and the recipe page shall show how to set that header.

criteria.doc: Framework recipe: a LangGraph agent instrumented with OpenLLMetry, verified end to end
criteria.text: The recipe page shall record the framework, instrumentation and exporter versions that were verified, the wire encoding, the semantic-convention revision, the span parent and child structure, how application, run and conversation identity are derived, what each dashboard tab shows for span-only data, and that this path observes an agent but cannot pause, stop or gate it.

criteria.doc: An OpenTelemetry sender knows what was kept
criteria.text: The system shall answer a telemetry export with success only after every accounting record in it has been written to the local store or deliberately refused, and when the store cannot confirm the write it shall answer with a retryable status and a retry delay, and shall not report the export as received.

criteria.doc: An OpenTelemetry sender knows what was kept
criteria.text: Where some items in an export are malformed and the rest are valid, the system shall store the valid items, answer success, and report to the sender how many items it refused; a body that cannot be decoded shall be refused as a whole with a non-retryable status; and a request from another machine without valid credentials shall be refused before its body is read.

criteria.doc: An OpenTelemetry sender knows what was kept
criteria.text: Re-delivery of a record, span or data point already received shall not change any stored total or the live view, and two separately reported model calls that differ in their own time or identifiers shall remain two records.

criteria.doc: An OpenTelemetry sender knows what was kept
criteria.text: The system shall report, per signal and since the receiver started, how many items it received, stored, refused, recognised as already stored, held only in the live view, skipped because another source already reports them, and asked the sender to retry, together with the time and category of the last successful and last failed intake and the number of refused unauthenticated requests; it shall state that it keeps no intake queue; and the report shall contain no record content and no credentials.

criteria.doc: An OpenTelemetry sender knows what was kept
criteria.text: A spending-limit pause on the observed agents shall not stop the system from receiving and storing telemetry, and exports received during such a pause shall be counted.

criteria.doc: An OpenTelemetry sender knows what was kept
criteria.text: Where a sender does not report a usage value, the system shall store it as unknown rather than zero, and a spend rollup shall state how many records in each group carried a cost and shall report no spend figure for a group in which none did.

criteria.doc: An OpenTelemetry sender knows what was kept
criteria.text: The spend rollup shall be computed from received log records alone, so that a sender sampling its traces does not reduce it.

criteria.doc: An OpenTelemetry sender knows what was kept
criteria.text: The generated ingest reference shall state the acknowledgement rule, each response status and whether the sender should retry it, the identity used to recognise a re-delivery for each signal, the session identity used when a sender provides none, and which received data is held only in the live view.
