criteria.doc: Self-Hosted Server Image: Signed, Pullable, Verified After Release
criteria.text: When an open-source release is published, the system shall publish a self-hosted server image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 to a public registry, built from the exact wheel published for that release after verifying that wheel's build provenance.

criteria.doc: Self-Hosted Server Image: Signed, Pullable, Verified After Release
criteria.text: The published image shall carry a keyless signature, an SBOM attestation bound to its digest, and a build provenance attestation, each verifiable by anyone without ClawMetry credentials.

criteria.doc: Self-Hosted Server Image: Signed, Pullable, Verified After Release
criteria.text: The image shall contain only the open-source package and its public dependencies, and shall not contain the proprietary Pro plugin.

criteria.doc: Self-Hosted Server Image: Signed, Pullable, Verified After Release
criteria.text: After publishing, the release pipeline shall pull the image by digest with no registry credentials on each published architecture, verify its signature and SBOM attestation, and fail naming the reason when the image cannot be pulled anonymously.

criteria.doc: Self-Hosted Server Image: Signed, Pullable, Verified After Release
criteria.text: The verification shall start the pulled image with persistent storage, send a non-sensitive event through the node ingest API from outside the container, restart the container, and confirm the event is still returned by the audit export and the node still appears on the fleet page.

criteria.doc: Self-Hosted Server Image: Signed, Pullable, Verified After Release
criteria.text: The same image build and persistence check shall run on every pull request that changes the image definition or its verification, against an image built from that branch, so a broken image is caught before a release.

criteria.doc: Self-Hosted Server Image: Signed, Pullable, Verified After Release
criteria.text: Only after verification passes, the system shall propose a change pinning the Compose deployment to the verified image by version and digest in place of the source build, and the Compose file shall never reference the published image by a tag alone.

criteria.doc: Self-Hosted Server Image: Signed, Pullable, Verified After Release
criteria.text: The self-hosting documentation shall state how to verify the signature and SBOM, how to update and roll back by digest, how to back up and restore, and the actual authentication and transport defaults, and shall mark deployment targets and identity integrations that have not been verified as not available.

criteria.doc: Self-Hosted Server Image: Signed, Pullable, Verified After Release
criteria.text: When the server runs in self-hosted mode, requests to the self-hosted server's own API routes shall be authorised by that server's node token or admin credentials regardless of the caller's network address, and shall not be refused for lacking a local gateway token.

criteria.doc: Self-Hosted Server Image: Signed, Pullable, Verified After Release
criteria.text: Every other API route shall keep the existing rule for non-loopback callers, and a self-hosted route called without its own credentials shall still be refused.

criteria.doc: LiteLLM gateway usage: spend by team and user, labelled and never double counted
criteria.text: When a LiteLLM proxy exports request telemetry to the receiver, the system shall record one usage record per proxied request, attributed to the team, user and virtual key that LiteLLM authenticated for that request.

criteria.doc: LiteLLM gateway usage: spend by team and user, labelled and never double counted
criteria.text: Team, user and organisation attribution shall come only from the identity LiteLLM derived from the authenticated key. Labels a caller supplies in the request body shall not change which team or user a request is attributed to.

criteria.doc: LiteLLM gateway usage: spend by team and user, labelled and never double counted
criteria.text: Each record shall retain the actual provider and model alongside the alias the caller requested, input and output token counts, whether the call streamed, whether it succeeded, its timestamps, and its trace, parent-span and provider response identifiers.

criteria.doc: LiteLLM gateway usage: spend by team and user, labelled and never double counted
criteria.text: Gateway spend shall be labelled as reported by the gateway, in the gateway's currency, and shall not be re-priced by ClawMetry or presented as a vendor invoice. When the gateway reports no cost for a request, that request shall be counted as having no reported cost, never as costing zero.

criteria.doc: LiteLLM gateway usage: spend by team and user, labelled and never double counted
criteria.text: Receiving the same exported request again shall not change any total. A request the gateway recorded as a separate request shall be counted separately.

criteria.doc: LiteLLM gateway usage: spend by team and user, labelled and never double counted
criteria.text: A response the gateway served from its own response cache, identified by carrying the same provider response identifier as an earlier request, shall be counted as a request but not charged a second time, whichever of the two arrives first.

criteria.doc: LiteLLM gateway usage: spend by team and user, labelled and never double counted
criteria.text: Gateway spend shall be presented as its own subtotal, shall not be added to agent runtime totals, and gateway requests shall not create agent sessions. The surface shall state how many gateway requests share a trace with telemetry from another source and how many could not be correlated.

criteria.doc: LiteLLM gateway usage: spend by team and user, labelled and never double counted
criteria.text: Failed gateway requests shall be counted per team and shown separately from successful ones.

criteria.doc: LiteLLM gateway usage: spend by team and user, labelled and never double counted
criteria.text: Team, user and key labels shall be displayed as text and never interpreted as markup.

criteria.doc: LiteLLM gateway usage: spend by team and user, labelled and never double counted
criteria.text: A real LiteLLM proxy at a pinned version, with two teams and two virtual keys backed by its own database, shall be exercised in continuous integration, and the per-team spend the system reports shall agree with LiteLLM's own spend log for the same requests, with any residual printed.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: When a tool result in a session contains text matching an injection signature, the system shall raise a `prompt_injection` finding that names the matched signature identifiers and the tool whose output carried the text, and shall not repeat the matched text.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: When a user-sourced message matches an injection signature, the system shall raise the finding with the source identified as a user message and at a lower severity than a tool-result match, unless a high-risk tool call followed it in the same turn.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: When a tool call rated high or critical risk follows the matched content in the same turn, the system shall raise the finding at critical severity and name that call's tool.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: The system shall offer `prompt_injection` to Guard policies like every other finding kind, and the finding shall carry its framework references (OWASP LLM01:2026, OWASP ASI01, MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051.000 and AML.T0051.001) under the mapping contract.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: When signature text appears as source code or a regular expression rather than prose, the system shall not raise a finding for it.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: The system shall publish the detector's recall and precision on pinned public prompt-injection samples and its firing rate on real transcripts, and continuous integration shall fail when the pinned recall falls below the published figure.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: When the Claude Code pre-tool gate rates a high-risk tool call and a tool result from an untrusted source entered the same turn before it, the system shall rate the call critical and shall say why in the risk reasons.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: When content earlier in the same turn matched an injection signature, the system shall rate a tool call of medium risk or above as critical.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: The system shall leave a low-risk call's tier unchanged, shall leave a medium-risk call's tier unchanged unless content in the turn matched an injection signature, and a new user prompt shall end the turn so earlier content no longer raises the tier.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: When the turn cannot be read, the system shall rate the call exactly as it would without this signal and shall never block a call because the context was unavailable.

criteria.doc: Guard Prompt Injection: a detector, and untrusted content raises the pre-tool risk tier
criteria.text: The context the gate hook sends to the local receiver shall carry tool names, counts and signature identifiers only, never tool output.
